title.narrative: Strengthening Development Impact through Evidence-Based Learning - DIF

description.narrative:
This agreement supports the Development Impact Fund (DIF) Umbrella Facility, a Multi-Donor Trust Fund in the World Bank aimed at increasing the impact of development finance by generating and applying rigorous and actionable research across development sectors at the global, national, and local levels. DIF seeks to promote the widespread use of science in policy making, foster ownership in the generation and adoption of evidence, and transition from financial reporting to reporting the causal impact of development finance. DIF aims to operate on the following guiding principles: • Enable countries to adopt analytically advanced digital management tools and conduct policy trials to help prioritize investments and inform programmatic choices. • Embrace coproduction between the government and its partners to expand local capacities for evidence-based policy making and generate contextually relevant solutions. • Expand knowledge financing and promote knowledge diffusion through country, sector, and global collaborations.
DIF addresses the problem of limited, unevenly distributed evidence for policymaking, aiming to enhance the impact of development programs. The core activities encompass: (1) Curation and production of multi-sector data to understand constraints and develop and evaluate potential solutions; (2) Rigorous Impact Evaluations to drive evidence-based policy organized in country/region/sector programs; and (3) Capacity building for evidence-based policymaking through coproduction with/and training of the government counterparts to leverage evidence.
DIF's research programs are organized into four main thematic pillars: People (education, gender, social protection), Planet (climate change, environment and natural resources, water), Proseprity (private sector, governance, public finance, trade) and Infrastructure (digital, energy, transport).
